entry.title: MAX POWER at NASA's Kennedy Space Center | Nov. 7-8, 2026

media:group.media:title: MAX POWER at NASA's Kennedy Space Center | Nov. 7-8, 2026
media:group.media:description:
America’s newest and most exciting aerospace technology expo and air show is landing at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, Nov. 7-8.
In honor of America’s 250th anniversary, NASA and external collaborators are hosting MAX POWER, a two-day air and space festival for families, aircraft and tech enthusiasts, and NASA fans of all ages to celebrate, explore, and be inspired. MAX POWER features air shows, tech displays, and astronaut appearances from some of our most famous missions.
Learn how to join us: www.nasa.gov/maxpower

media:group.media:title: 2026 Total Solar Eclipse
media:group.media:description:
Come watch the eclipse with NASA.
On Wednesday, Aug. 12, a total solar eclipse will be visible in parts of Greenland, Iceland, Spain, and the Atlantic Ocean. A partial solar eclipse will be visible in most of Europe and parts of North America.
Totality will begin in Iceland at 1:45 p.m. EDT (1745 UTC) and in Spain at 2:28 p.m. EDT (1828 UTC).
Can't see it where you are? We'll be streaming live views from a number of cameras in the path of the eclipse — and sharing info about the science of eclipses and how we're studying them.
More info on our live coverage: https://go.nasa.gov/3TvNDAd Learn more about eclipses: https://science.nasa.gov/eclipses/

media:group.media:title: U.S. Spacewalk 97
media:group.media:description:
At approximately 8:35 a.m. EDT (1235 UTC) on Aug. 18, 2026, NASA astronaut Anil Menon and ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot will venture outside the International Space Station for an approximately six-and-a-half-hour spacewalk. The pair will replace a Space-to-Ground antenna that enables high-speed communications between the Mission Control Center in Houston and the orbital complex.
This spacewalk will be Menon’s second and Adenot’s first. Adenot will become the first French woman to conduct a spacewalk.
Learn more about this spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4x9ASdi Read the latest mission updates from the station: https://nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
Credit: NASA

media:group.media:title: U.S. Spacewalk 96
media:group.media:description:
At approximately 8:35 a.m. EDT (1235 UTC) on Aug. 6, 2026, NASA astronauts Anil Menon and Jessica Meir will venture outside the International Space Station for an approximately six-and-a-half-hour spacewalk. The pair will install hardware that will modify the station’s 3B power channel and prepare it for the future installation of an International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array.
This spacewalk will be the first for Menon and the sixth for Meir. Meir will serve as spacewalk crew member 1 and will wear a suit with red stripes. Menon will serve as crew member 2 and will wear an unmarked suit.
Learn more about this spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4x9ASdi Read the latest mission updates from the station: https://nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
Credit: NASA

media:group.media:title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams Postflight News Conference (Aug. 4, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
Tune in as astronaut Chris Williams recaps his eight-month mission aboard the International Space Station.
After logging 241 days aboard the orbital laboratory, Williams returned to Earth on July 26, 2026. During his mission, he contributed to a wide range of scientific investigations and technology demonstrations, including research on new cancer treatments and manufacturing materials used in high-performance computers and electronics.
Learn more about the science Williams conducted: https://go.nasa.gov/4fjNCry Learn more about the International Space Station: https://www.nasa.gov/station
Credit: NASA

entry.title: Live Video from the International Space Station (Official NASA Stream)

media:group.media:title: Live Video from the International Space Station (Official NASA Stream)
media:group.media:description:
Watch live video from the International Space Station, including inside views when the crew aboard the space station is on duty. Views of Earth are also streamed from an external camera located outside of the space station. During periods of signal loss due to handover between communications satellites, a blue screen is displayed.
The space station orbits Earth about 250 miles (425 kilometers) above the surface. An international partnership of five space agencies from 15 countries operates the station, and it has been continuously occupied since November 2000. It's a microgravity laboratory where science, research, and human innovation make way for new technologies and research breakthroughs not possible on Earth. More: https://go.nasa.gov/3CkVtC8
Did you know you can spot the station without a telescope? It looks like a fast-moving star, but you have to know when to look up. Download our mobile app for alerts to let you know when (and where) to spot the station and wave to the crew: https://www.nasa.gov/spot-the-station/
https://nasa.gov/iss
